analysis.investment_thesis: Aurionpro is a genuine turnaround — revenue tripled since FY21 and margins are expanding — but at 25x trailing P/E and a FCF yield of just 1.2% (FCF INR 62 Cr on MCap INR 5,094 Cr), the price already reflects continued strong growth, leaving virtually no margin of safety. The M&A-driven growth strategy (investing outflows of INR 421 Cr in FY25, funded by equity dilution) embeds integration risk that consensus appears to be discounting entirely.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.02, net cash INR 239 Cr) means no distress risk even if growth disappoints
Consistent EBITDA expansion: INR 128 Cr (FY20) → INR 262 Cr (FY25), a ~15% 5-year CAGR with operating margin holding at 17%+
Diversified, sticky revenue mix across banking tech, govt/smart city, and data-center — multiple growth engines reduce concentration risk
key_risks: M&A execution risk: INR 421 Cr invested in FY25 alone funded by equity raises (financing CF +INR 283 Cr); acquisition integration is unproven at this scale
FCF conversion is poor — FY25 FCF of INR 62 Cr is only 33% of net profit of INR 188 Cr; rising capex (INR 95 Cr in FY25 vs INR 32 Cr prior year) signals heavy investment phase
Low promoter stake of 26.88% reduces alignment with minority shareholders; FII ownership at 16% creates exit-flow vulnerability in a risk-off environment
red_flags: Massive equity dilution: total equity surged from INR 337 Cr (FY21) to INR 1,606 Cr (FY25), far exceeding cumulative retained earnings of ~INR 509 Cr — significant shareholder base expansion
FY21 impairment crisis: net loss of INR 192 Cr on 'Other Income' of -INR 118 Cr reveals historical goodwill/asset write-downs, raising questions about past M&A quality
FY25 investing outflow of INR 421 Cr against OCF of only INR 157 Cr — the company is consuming far more cash than it generates organically, bridged entirely by capital markets
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The second-level question here is not "is Aurionpro a better business than in 2021?" — it clearly is. The question is what the price already reflects. At EV/EBITDA of 18.4x on INR 262 Cr EBITDA, the market is embedding ~47% forward earnings growth (implied by P/E 25x vs. forward P/E 16.9x). That growth must come largely from recently acquired assets, since organic OCF of INR 157 Cr against a INR 5,094 Cr market cap yields just 3.1% — inadequate for a risk-bearing investor. For context, the 9-year revenue CAGR is only 5.7%, and the recent acceleration is largely acquisition-fueled, not organic outperformance.

The stress scenario is the critical lens. If EBITDA growth decelerates to 10-12% (still respectable) and the market re-rates to 12x EV/EBITDA — a reasonable trough for Indian mid-cap IT — implied EV would be ~INR 3,144 Cr, against the current ~INR 4,855 Cr EV (MCap less net cash). That is ~35% downside. With FCF yield at 1.2% providing no income buffer, holders are entirely dependent on multiple expansion or sustained 20%+ earnings growth. That is not asymmetric risk/reward in my framework — it is symmetric at best, and unfavorable when the cycle turns. Hold if already owned with low cost basis; new capital finds better risk-adjusted entries elsewhere.
